name: credits-meter
title: Credits Meter
description: What's left, and what this will cost — before the click. Takes the `remaining` balance and optional `allowance`, both formatted by you, a measured `used` proportion, a `nextAction` naming the action and its `cost` together with `affordable` when it exceeds the balance, `resets` for when the balance renews or expires, `recent` for movement including refunds, `low` to mark a balance worth flagging, and `onTopUp`. The pairing of action and price is the point: buyers of these tools rank credit opacity as their first frustration, and the specific complaint is that you cannot tell what an action will cost until it has been spent. Purely presentational: you compute the numbers and format the units. Use it beside a generate button, in a studio's sidebar, or above a batch. Not a billing page, and not a place for raw token counts — convert to the unit your users are charged in.

meta.engineeringNotes: `nextAction` is a single object rather than separate label and cost props so the two can never be rendered apart: a price with no action, or an action with no price, is the pattern the component exists to replace. `affordable` is a caller flag instead of something derived from parsing the strings, because balances and costs arrive as formatted text in whatever unit and locale the product uses, and a component that tried to compare them would have to parse money. The bar is drawn only from a measured `used` value, which keeps it consistent with the rest of the system's rule that a proportion must be real, and it draws what is *left* rather than what is spent: it sits under a figure that counts down, and a bar filling up beside a balance running out reads as plenty-left at the exact moment it is not. Refunds get a place in `recent` because generation pipelines refund routinely and almost no interface shows it, which leaves people believing failures cost them money.
meta.motionNotes: Nothing animates. A balance is a fact and the next action's price is a decision point, so neither has anything to express through motion; only the standard instant colour change on the top-up button, disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

remaining.description: What's left, formatted by you: "1,250 credits", "$18.40".

allowance.description: The full allowance, when there is one: "2,000 credits this month".

used.description:
How much of the allowance is already spent, 0–1, measured. Renders a bar; leave it
out when you only have words. The bar draws what is *left*, so it empties as the
figure beside it falls.

nextAction.description:
What the next action will take, named and priced: the thing reviewers say is missing
everywhere. "4 images · 40 credits".

resets.description: When the balance resets or expires, in plain words: "Resets on 1 October".

recent.description: Recent movement, including refunds: "12 refunded yesterday when a batch failed".

low.description: Set when the balance is low enough to say so.

docs: Requires `cn` at `@/lib/utils`. Keep `nextAction.label` specific to the click it sits beside: '8 images · 1024 × 1024', not 'Generate'.
